articles.headline: Orioles' Pete Alonso reaches 40 home runs on son's birthday
articles.description: Orioles slugger Pete Alonso threw a birthday bash for son Teddy as he turned 1, changing his walk-up music and hitting home runs No. 39 and 40 in a victory vs. Toronto.
articles.body:
Baltimore Orioles slugger Pete Alonso threw a birthday bash for son Teddy as he turned 1 on Monday, changing his walk-up music and, for the icing on the cake, hitting home runs No. 39 and 40 in a 4-3 victory against the Toronto Blue Jays.

Sept. 21st will be a day and night for the Alonso family to remember, indeed.

For starters, Alonso and his wife Haley began the day with a celebration at home, complete with presents and a large "Happy Birthday Theodore" banner.

Once he got to the ballpark, Alonso got right to work in the first inning. After walking from the batter's box to the plate to Dire Straits' "Money for Nothing," per normal, Alonso blasted No. 39 to right field.

He changed his tune in the eighth inning, however. In a one-time exception to celebrate Teddy, Alonso asked for "September" from Earth, Wind & Fire to be played.

Alonso then launched a a two-run blast to become the first Orioles player since Anthony Santander in 2024 to reach 40 home runs in a season.

"That's for him. That's his birthday song," Alonso told reporters. "Sick. It's 100% special, Hopefully, we can bookmark this game. I know it doesn't matter now, because he's not going to understand it for a couple years. But hopefully, a couple years down the line, I can kind of look back and just kind of bookmark this and keep it for the archives, and then hopefully, he appreciates it one day."

Alonso leads the American League with 108 RBIs.

"His baseball card, his accolades, the track record is there," manager Craig Albernaz said. "Hitting 40 home runs and having over 100 RBIs in this league is really impressive and the consistency he does it, that doesn't happen by accident. Just all the work he puts in behind the scenes."

With a new team and a newborn son, Alonso admitted it took some time this season to get into his usual rhythm.

"I think the hardest thing was navigating parenthood. It's like, 'How do we get this down?' Being husband, being dad, and then also being ready to my maximum capabilities by first pitch," Alonso said. "Just a couple routine tweaks, and I feel like as the season has gone on, I feel like I've just been able to kind of refine that and get more and more in tune and in rhythm.

"Really thankful for my teammates sticking with me. Really thankful for my wife."

articles.headline: 2026 NFL pass rush, run stop, blocking win rate rankings
articles.description: Our win rate metrics stack the NFL's top teams and players in run blocking, run stopping, pass protection and pass rushing.
articles.body:
ESPN Analytics created revolutionary metrics to measure performance in the trenches -- in both the run and pass game -- using player tracking data from NFL Next Gen Stats. And we updated the formula a little bit for 2026 -- see what's new here.

Our pass rush win rate metric tells us how often a pass rusher is able to beat/win his block within 2.5 seconds. Likewise, our pass block win rate metric conveys the rate linemen can sustain their blocks for 2.5 seconds or longer.

In run stop win rate, a defender can earn a win by doing any of the following: beating his blocker so he's in better position to stop the runner; disrupting the pocket or running lane by pushing his blocker backward; containing the runner such that he must adjust his running lane; or recording a tackle within 3 yards of the line of scrimmage. If a defender earns a run stop win, his blocker earns a loss -- and vice versa.

Here are the rankings for each metric for the 2026 NFL season.

articles.headline: Paul Skenes says WBC contributed to velocity drop in 2026
articles.description: Pirates ace Paul Skenes, whose season has been marked by an uncharacteristic dip in velocity, cited the World Baseball Classic as a source of his struggles this year.
articles.headlineJa: ポール・スキーンズ、2026年の球速低下はWBCが一因と明かす
articles.descriptionJa: 今季らしくない球速低下が目立つパイレーツのエース、ポール・スキーンズは、今年苦戦している原因としてワールド・ベースボール・クラシック（WBC）を挙げた。
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Pirates ace Paul Skenes, whose season has been marked by an uncharacteristic dip in velocity, cited the World Baseball Classic as a source of his struggles this year.

Skenes discussed his disappointing 2026 season with the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette, saying that the WBC was "kind of the root" of the diminished velocity that plagued him in recent months.

"There are a lot of other factors, so I don't want to put everything on [the WBC]," Skenes told the Post-Gazette as part of a wide-ranging interview published Monday. "But I feel like that was kind of the root of it a little bit."

Skenes' average fastball velocity this season was 96.8 mph, down from 98.1 mph last season and 98.8 mph in 2024.

The three-time All-Star's four-seam fastball dropped to a career-low 95.7 mph in a start last month against the Miami Marlins and averaged just 96.1 mph in his most recent start Friday against the Kansas City Royals.

Although he acknowledged mechanical adjustments that also contributed to his performance, Skenes mentioned the impact that the early-March WBC had on his annual ramp-up routine.

"Usually, that time of year, you're kind of ramping up and it's a little bit slow," he told the Post-Gazette. "You can kind of get onto the slope and find your body. One live [batting practice], you're topping at 97, and then the next you're 98, 99.

"And that wasn't the case this year. ... Looking back, I don't think that really helped."

Skenes, 24, is 10-11 with a 3.91 ERA and has 192 strikeouts in 168 innings over 31 starts this season. He won the National League Cy Young Award last year, when he boasted a major-league-best 1.97 ERA, and was the NL Rookie of the Year in 2024, when he had a 1.96 ERA.

Skenes revealed that he didn't feel 100% mechanically even early this season, when he was still posting his usual dominant numbers -- including a 1.09 ERA during an eight-start stretch in April and May.

"Even then, I didn't feel like I had my delivery," he said. "It's just weird. It's easier to kind of put your finger on it after the fact than it is in the moment."

Skenes said he expects to regain his mechanics ahead of the 2027 season. He emphasized that he doesn't regret representing Team USA, but added that the WBC "affected" his season with the Pirates.

"It definitely affected the year," he said. "Unfortunately, I don't think I'm the only one. ... Yeah, I don't know. [The WBC] definitely didn't make things easier."

articles.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba shows no signs of slowing down as Bobby Okereke silences critics
articles.description: Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba had arguably the best game of his career to date in the second week of the NFL season as he continued his bid for a second straight Offensive Player of the Year (OPOY) prize.
articles.headlineJa: 勢いが止まらないジャクソン・スミス＝ンジグバ、ボビー・オケレケは批判を黙らせる
articles.descriptionJa: シアトル・シーホークスのワイドレシーバー、ジャクソン・スミス＝ンジグバは、NFL第2週でキャリア最高とも言えるパフォーマンスを見せ、2年連続の最優秀攻撃選手賞（OPOY）獲得に向け前進を続けている。
articles.body:
Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba had arguably the best game of his career to date in the second week of the NFL season as he continued his bid for a second straight Offensive Player of the Year (OPOY) prize.

The wide receiver with ties to Sierra Leone through his grandparents possesses quality that was never in doubt after he led the Seattle Seahawks to the Super Bowl in February. However, Carolina Panthers linebacker Bobby Okereke - another player with ties to Africa through his Nigerian parents - had plenty to prove after his move from the New York Giants. So far, he has proved a shrewd acquisition. African Player of the Week: Jaxon Smith-Njigba (Seattle Seahawks)

Smith-Njigba scored a career record 82-yard touchdown in the Seahawks' 31-7 win over the Arizona Cardinals.

That play off the Seahawks' opening offensive drive set the tone for what was to come as JSN went on to score further touchdowns in the third and fourth quarter. He linked up with Drew Lock for three of the Seahawks' four touchdowns. AJ Barner then went over late on to put the cherry on top of the icing.

Smith-Njigba ended up with a total of 155 yards across nine receptions and his early touchdown beat his previous career best by 19 yards. African Moment of the Week: Bobby Okereke (Carolina Panthers)

In fairness, Smith-Njigba's performance against the Cardinals was sublime enough to be dissected from top to bottom of this Africa wrap. However, it would be a disservice to overlook Okereke's impressive display in the Panthers' 34-3 drubbing of the Atlanta Falcons.

He showed tremendously slick hands on an interception during the first quarter. The former Stanford star's reflexes were put to the test as he latched onto a Cooper Rush pass which had been diverted towards him off Devin Lloyd.

Okereke's contribution to the cause did not end there. Although replay assistance overturned what would have been his second interception of the half, he ended with nine tackles - six of which were solo tackles - and a quarterback hit.

The 30-year-old's talent has never been in doubt, but if there were question marks over his consistency with the Giants, he has gone a long way towards putting them to bed in his first two games for the Panthers. Although the Chicago Bears clash in Week 1 ended in defeat for the Panthers despite Okereke's forced fumble, he now has his first win for his new team. Honorable mentions:

Kingsley Enagbare - who like Okereke is of Nigerian descent - impressed with a sack and a forced fumble for the New York Jets against the Green Bay Packers, with whom he started his career. However, he ended up on the losing side against his old team as the Jets went down 20-17.

Emeka Egbuka - whose father is Nigerian - got off to a strong start with a touchdown for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers against the Cleveland Browns. However, his game ended in heartbreak as he and Baker Mayfield failed to connect late on for what could have been a game-winner.

articles.headline: Benjamin Šeško vows to 'fully dedicate' himself to recovery after Man United injury setback
articles.description: Manchester United striker Benjamin Sesko has vowed to "fully dedicate" himself to his recovery from an ongoing shin issue.
articles.headlineJa: マンUで怪我に見舞われたベンヤミン・シェシュコ、回復に「全力を尽くす」と誓う
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・ユナイテッドのストライカー、ベンヤミン・シェシュコは、続いているすねの傷みの回復に「全力を尽くす」と誓った。
articles.body:
Manchester United striker Benjamin Šeško has vowed to "fully dedicate" himself to his recovery from an ongoing shin issue.

The 23-year-old moved to Old Trafford from RB Leipzig last August in a deal worth 76.5million euros (£66.3m/$88.6m) plus 8.5m euros (£7.4m/$9.9m) in potential add-ons.

Šeško scored 12 goals during a promising first campaign that was brought to an abrupt end by a shin injury in May, which ruled him out of all of United's preseason friendlies.

The striker managed to play a part in the first six games of the season, scoring twice, only for the recurrence of shin pain to rule him out of Sunday's 1-1 draw at Fulham and international duty with Slovenia.

"I am very sorry that I will have to miss the next matches of the national team," Sesko posted on Instagram.

"I have always played for Slovenia and will always play with heart and pride. The most important thing now is to fully dedicate myself to recovery.

"I am already working on getting back on the field as soon as possible and helping the national team and the club again.

"I believe in our boys, and I am sure that they will show the team spirit that has always adorned us this time.

"I can't wait to be able to wear the jersey with the national emblem again and, until then, I will be Slovenia's biggest fan."

Slovenia host Scotland on Saturday and end the three-week international break with a trip to Hampden Park, with a home clash against North Macedonia and a trip to Switzerland in between, as the Nations League gets under way.

United are not back in action until Oct. 10, when fellow strugglers Tottenham head to Old Trafford, before tough-looking trips to Atletico Madrid, Leeds and Como.

- Kylian Mbappé on past Liverpool transfer talks: 'Mum went to Anfield and fell in love'

- Cole Palmer, Declan Rice withdraw from England's Nations League squad

Šeško's absence for those matches would be a major blow given Michael Carrick's side failed to sign another out-and-out striker during the summer.

Asked whether United should have done so, given the current situation, the head coach said after the Fulham match: "No, I think that just because you get setbacks in certain positions, you can't sign a player for cover in every one.

"We're not sure with Ben yet, he felt some pain after the game [against Brighton in the Carabao Cup] and we are assessing him at the moment.

"He definitely wasn't ready for [Sunday]. I haven't got any more news to give you, just that he felt pain on his shin."

Šeško is one of four United players to have withdrawn from international duty. Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford pulled out of the England squad, while Karl Darlow did not not join up with Wales.

The Premier League club said: "Each of the players will be assessed and undergo individual recovery plans during the current three-week international break."

articles.headline: Silver linings for MLB's 2026 non-playoff teams
articles.description: Your favorite team won't be playing in October -- but that doesn't mean the season was a total loss. Right?
articles.headlineJa: 2026年MLBプレーオフを逃したチームにとっての「希望の光」
articles.descriptionJa: 応援しているチームが10月にプレーしないとしても、シーズン全体が完全な失敗だったわけではありません。そうですよね？
articles.body:
So your team missed the playoffs. There are worse things, right? Their 2026 MLB season is ending in disappointment, but there are some positives, too. There always are, in every team's campaign, even if they might not always be readily apparent. Not everything has gone wrong.

As the proverb goes, every cloud has a silver lining, a 19th-century saying that has its roots in "Comus", a 1634 poem by John Milton, no relation to Eric. Little known fact, but Milton -- the one who wrote "Paradise Lost" -- wasn't much of a baseball guy.

Some baseball loyalists -- we'll call them "Mets fans" -- tend to fixate on the clouds. Others -- we'll call them "Brooklyn Dodgers fans" -- zero right in on the silver lining and start saying things like, "Wait till next year!"

For teams that have already crossed the mathematical elimination threshold in 2026, the wait for next year begins after the regular-season games are over Sunday. But even those teams head home buoyed by some kind of silver lining, one that hopefully will imbue the looming winter vigil with a hint of anticipation for the inevitable spring to come.

Jump to:

American League | National League

American League

Athletics

Silver lining: Henry Bolte

After a promising start, the Athletics imploded under the dual pressures of injury and underperformance. All of this makes silver-lining hunting more difficult, especially if we don't want to play the "at least they're one year closer to Vegas" card.

Still, Bolte looks like a keeper. He's a walking toolkit with a range of raw skills that includes an MLB-leading sprint speed and 95th percentile bat speed. Despite a raw plate approach that features too much swing and miss, he has still managed a .272/.357/.396 line that for a 22-year-old is bursting with promise.

Add a version of Bolte that improves in his second year to a lineup full of 2026 disappointments ripe for a collective bounce-back, and the Athletics might get back on track quickly, at least on offense. As for the pitching ... we're silver lining people today.

Detroit Tigers

Silver lining: Kevin McGonigle is who we thought he'd be

The Tigers have turned out a few highly rated prospects in recent years, but if you reference prospect ratings for Detroit from four and five years ago, you see a lot of players who have struggled to establish themselves, have gotten hurt, have fallen short or are succeeding for other teams.

On the current roster, Riley Greene remains a cornerstone player, but his rise has been a slow burn. Not so for McGonigle, who entered the season as one of the game's top prospects and has been even better than advertised, right from the very first game.

McGonigle is not only the best rookie in baseball in 2026, he arguably has had the best first season by a Tigers hitter in more than a century. Sometimes hype isn't just hype.

Kansas City Royals

Silver lining: Carter Jensen and Jac Caglianone established themselves as regulars
